note: Batch 1 broad survey of raw base features across lookbacks to map which signal families carry sign and magnitude in this panel
Batch 2 maps full lookback response curves for kurtosis vol skew and correlation families to separate smooth structure from single lucky parameters
Batch 3 tests normalizations neighbour-averaging and cross-family composites of the kurtosis low-vol and long-horizon momentum families
Batch 4 systematic composite search combining kurtosis blends short horizon momentum long horizon momentum and low vol

text: Approach: map signal families broadly first, then prefer structures that show smooth lookback response curves over single lucky parameters. Findings so far: (1) cross-sectional return kurtosis is the dominant effect, positive with a smooth hump peaking near 10-20 days and decaying to negative by 250 days - the sign is stable across 5,10,15,20,40,60 so it is structural not noise; (2) low volatility and low beta anomalies are present and sign-stable at every lookback but individually weak, SR 0.2-0.6; (3) momentum is two-regime - positive at 3-15 days and at 250 days, negative at 40-120 days. Key robustness result: blending multiple kurtosis lookbacks via cs_z sums improves SR monotonically (1.20 single -> 1.55 three-way), which is estimation-noise diversification rather than parameter mining, so it should survive out of sample. Time-series normalization ts_z of kurtosis DEGRADES it, confirming the effect is a cross-sectional characteristic, not a timing signal. Short-horizon momentum ret(10) is complementary to kurtosis, lifting rank IC from 0.0066 to 0.0083. Deliberately avoiding multiplicative interactions, which scored near zero, and avoiding narrow parameter picks in favour of averaged ensembles.

text: Final selection logic. The search converged on one economically coherent structure: a cross-sectional composite of (a) a multi-lookback return-kurtosis ensemble, (b) a short-horizon momentum sleeve at 10 days, and (c) an embedded low-volatility tilt introduced by dividing the longer kurtosis terms by trailing vol. All three ingredients were independently validated before being combined - kurtosis is positive and sign-stable at 5,10,15,20,40,60 with a smooth hump peaking near 15; volatility is negatively related to forward returns at every one of the nine lookbacks tested; 10-day momentum is positive with neighbours at 3 and 15 days also positive. Crucially the final train SR surface is a broad flat plateau, not a spike: roughly forty distinct parameterisations score between 1.95 and 2.06, and every single-parameter perturbation of the chosen signals stays above 2.00. I deliberately did NOT report the single highest train SR point, since on a flat plateau the argmax is the most upward-biased estimate. Instead I picked three members near the plateau centre that differ in their short kurtosis lookback (3 versus 5), their vol-scaling denominators (5, 10, 60) and their mix of raw versus vol-scaled kurtosis terms, so that parameter-specific estimation error is spread across the three reported signals. Rejected along the way: multiplicative interactions of z-scores, which scored near zero; time-series z-scoring of kurtosis, which cut SR by two thirds and showed the effect is a cross-sectional characteristic not a timing signal; and adding long-horizon momentum, correlation or skew as a fifth sleeve, each of which reduced SR by 0.3 to 0.5 despite being positive standalone. Signal decays materially under a 5-day delay so it is a moderately fast signal, and all scores here are gross of costs.
